newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NatMut says not seeking bank purchase.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NatMut says not seeking bank purchase.

text.p: Life insurance group National Mutual Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it was not interested in buying an Australian bank, despite its ongoing push into the Australian home lending market which is dominated by banks.

"National Mutual is not interested in getting into core banking. We have no interest whatsoever in participating in any rationalisation of the banking industry in this country," managing director Geoff Tomlinson told a Committee for the Economic Development of Australia (CEDA) luncheon meeting.

National Mutual, as part of its submission to the government's financial system inquiry, has called for the lifting of individual shareholding limits contained in the Bank Shareholding Act and Insurance (Takeovers and Acquisitions) Act.

Tomlinson said the group's home lending division was expected to write about A$1 billion worth of new business in the year to September 30, 1997. He said the division, which has been in existence for about 18 months, has written about A$750 million worth of loans so far. "Our strategy is to be cautious to begin with...we are relatively small," Tomlinson said.

National Mutual's home loans are seeded by industry superannuation funds. Tomlinson said National Mutual also was entering the commercial lending market but said it was yet to build its lending book to a size that justified securitisation.
National Mutual is 51 percent owned by AXA SA of France.
At 0417 GMT (03.18 p.m.) National Mutual shares were down four cents at A$1.75.
